facts.fact: The World Bank's ID4D diagnostic of May 2026 states that the national civil registration system is in practice largely non-existent, that birth registration is yet to be implemented and that birth certificates do not exist, with about 90 percent of births unrecorded in any official register; the finding is undated, so the published month is used.

The World Bank's May 2026 diagnostic lists the DCRNPI Civil Registration System as planned only, and says birth registration is yet to be implemented; births may be declared at civil registration or identification offices within 45 days but this is uncommon in practice. No office is described as registering digitally; the published month is used as the date.
The World Bank's May 2026 systems table gives DCRNPI as operator and owner of the planned Civil Registration System, meant as the integrated national data source under the 2024 ID Regulations.

The World Bank's May 2026 diagnostic says implementation of the civil registration and identification framework has been complicated by limited institutional capacity and insufficient funding; it names no budget line or donor for the planned civil registration system.

The World Bank's May 2026 diagnostic says plans exist to improve interoperability through the civil registry as the national data source but progress remains slow, and that implementation of the legal framework remains extremely limited.
